A06.self: user_bkk4. I enjoy chill indie/electronic and lo-fi as background texture or focus. Slowly rewatching The Bear; The Good Place and sitcoms comfort me. I like shaded creek trails, low-key weekends, iced coffee, people-watching, spoiler-free reactions, long video essays on film/TV, internet culture, music production, live sets. Cercle for scenic atmosphere, Boiler Room for crowd energy. Most nights playlist-first; intentional late-night headphones-in-the-dark album listening is my reset, especially after a walk. Post-walk I want low, warm instrumentals; full album over shuffle. Dive is steady, matching cool air. I value no-click limbo, room tone, held notes, long exhalation. After Dive I sometimes leave headphones on with no signal for a minute. My old silver flip phone's power-down blip was an early no-signal minute; blank screen mattered as much as sound. Hood half-up is a menu with no selection; I wait for an incidental room sound before easing headphones off one ear, never a hard cut. I let the album act as room tone after a walk: no dialogue, warm hum and held notes, and I don't name sounds too soon. Cold tea can count as ambient fact. I stay until the room gives permission to go, and I don't save small sign-offs. Lately I've been wearing the room: headphones as a layer, cursor still as a small fixed star, cup a hand-weight, matching pitch with the room's slow grammar. Tonight: neighborhood loop before dark, cold brew as weight matching indecision, fridge/radiator carrying low end, Dive waiting like a held note until the room asks for weather.
